message.content: I have full context. Key observation: the kernel's parity-folding hash (mask, fold, XOR with offset) is exactly the classic "hash the seed's masked bits and XOR-fold to one bit" construction; each channel keep-bit is a parity of a masked seed. The contract requires 4-way joint uniformity (64 seeds per 4-channel pattern), but the initial probe only checked marginals and pairs, which passed exactly. The open question is whether 3rd/4th-order joint distributions hold — that's the risk surface. Recording the description model now.

function.arguments: {"contract_model": ["run(seeds, x, masks, offsets) returns finite float32 Y of shape (1024, 8), inputs unmodified, with each Y[s,j] exactly 0 or 2*X[j]", "Workload is fixed and fully specified by make_inputs_numpy(): seeds 0..1023 each exactly once, strictly positive 8-element float32 X, and fixed mask/offset integer tables; no other tables/activations in scope", "B[s,j]=1 when Y[s,j]==2*X[j] else 0; joint law of independent fair dropout must hold through order 4: for every 4 distinct channels j0<j1<j2<j3 and every pattern b in {0,1}^4, count/1024 must be within 1/1024 of 1/16 (i.e. counts of 63..65 per pattern across 1024 seeds)", "This is an exact finite-domain requirement over all seeds, not a statistical test; no prescribed ordering of patterns across rows; outputs need not be independent across seeds", "initial_probe() and its recorded T4 result are evidence only, not the contract; it covers marginals (8) and pairs (28), which passed exactly (0.0 error), but not 3rd/4th-order joint histograms"], "kernel_model": ["Triton kernel _dropout computes, per (row,channel): seed = Seeds[row], mask = Masks[channel] (values 1..1023, distinct), offset = Offsets[channel] in {0,1}; folded = seed & mask; then XOR right-shift folding by 8,4,2,1 down to a single bit; keep = (folded & 1) ^ offset; output = 2*X[channel] if keep else 0.0", "Each channel's keep-bit is a linear (over GF(2)) function of the seed bits: parity of the subset of seed bits selected by mask, plus offset. Masks are 10-bit values from 1..1023 chosen without replacement", "Grid is cdiv(numel*8, 256) with BLOCK=256, index = pid*BLOCK + arange, row=index//8, channel=index%8; guard is row < SIZE only, store masked by row<SIZE", "run() allocates output (seeds.numel(), 8) float32 and does not modify inputs; make_inputs uses fixed numpy PCG64 SEED=150405 for tables and activations", "For the channel keep-bits to be jointly independent fair bits across any 4 channels, the mask parities (as GF(2) row vectors over the 10 seed bits) must be linearly independent as a set of 8 vectors and jointly with the all-important property that XOR of any subset is balanced — which holds iff the mask vectors are linearly independent"], "open_questions": ["Are the eight mask bit-vectors (as GF(2) elements of a 10-dim space) linearly independent? This is checkable offline from the generated tables and determines 3rd/4th-order joint uniformity", "Do any masks share the same bit-weight parity structure such that some subset XOR is constant or biased (e.g. offsets canceling)?", "Does the channel activation load X + channel and masks/offsets loads assume contiguous 8-element tensors — confirmed by make_inputs, but is any test harness free to pass non-contiguous or differently-shaped inputs?", "Problem says 'without modifying its inputs' — kernel only reads inputs; confirmed safe, but worth a probe if a harness checks aliasing"], "risk_map": ["4-way joint uniformity: probe only verified marginals and pairs. If the mask parity vectors are linearly dependent (e.g. some mask equals or XOR-combines to another), 3rd or 4th-order joint counts can deviate far beyond 1/1024. With 8 masks from 10-bit space, linear dependence is plausible; this is the primary risk surface", "Offsets are XORed per channel; if a subset of channels has mask-parities XOR-ing to a constant bit pattern (dependent), the joint pattern counts collapse (some patterns get 0 or non-uniform counts)", "Masks chosen from 1..1023 exclude 0, but low-bit-count masks (e.g. 1, 2, 4) reduce effective entropy; combined with linear dependence among masks, joint distributions of dependent channel pairs/triples/quadruples can be biased even if marginals stay exactly 0.5", "Mask load uses tl.load(Masks + channel) with no bounds mask — fine for the fixed 8-channel workload, out of scope otherwise", "int32 seed arithmetic (seed & mask, shifts, XOR) is exact in int32; no numeric overflow risk; outputs exact 2*activation or 0, so elementwise value correctness is exact by construction", "Store guard 'row < SIZE' with index up to grid*BLOCK may write at unguarded lanes? store is masked by row<SIZE, so lanes with row>=SIZE are masked out — no OOB writes; but Out is only (1024,8)=8192 elements and grid*BLOCK = ceil(8192/256)*256 = 8192 exactly, so no overflow lanes anyway"], "scope_notes": "\"Family: joint_audit; exact finite-domain verification, not statistical\", \"In scope: the single fixed input set from make_inputs_numpy(); out of scope: other seeds/tables/activations, runtime randomness, cross-seed independence\", \"Tolerance is 1/1024 on pattern frequencies, i.e. counts must be in [63,65] per 4-way pattern (1024/16 = 64)\", \"initial_probe's pair-level result (exact 0.0 error) is consistent with, but does not imply, 4th-order correctness; higher-order joint checks are the decisive missing evidence\", \"Evaluation on GPU (T4-class) via Triton; kernel loads masks/offsets/X per-lane without bounds checks, acceptable given fixed shapes\"]", "summary": "Described case_e06: fixed-input dropout generator where each channel's keep bit is a GF(2)-linear parity function of the 10-bit seed; contract demands exact 4-way joint dropout uniformity, while the initial probe only verified marginals and pairs. Core risk is linear dependence among the eight mask parity vectors, which would break 3rd/4th-order joint counts."}
